clue.text: Made inroads before cold gets bitter

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come before the next piece in the answer
the letters of inroads are made into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An army that has made inroads into enemy territory meets a cold, bitter spell of weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made inroads' reads as a phrase meaning advanced, but 'Made' is the anagram signal: INROADS rearranged gives SARDONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic humour is grimly mocking and cynical, a synonym for bitter in tone.

clue.text: How no-one concludes part of the day

parts.note: written out, no-one is the letters NOON followed by a final E, so the word finishes with an E placed after the middle of the day

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a nobody ends up, followed by a stray phrase about the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell no-one without the hyphen: NOON then E. So it concludes just past noon, which gives the time of day as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The period between midday and evening is one portion of a day.

clue.text: Fear uncoiling adder

indicators.note: a snake uncoiling changes its shape, so the letters of adder are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A snake slowly uncoiling inspires fear in whoever sees it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is deep fear or apprehension; as a noun or verb the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Beans go rotten in food container

indicators.note: rotten beans have gone bad and lost their form, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beans that have gone off are left in a container meant for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's feed bag hung over its head holds its food, so it is a food container.

clue.text: Clever to support clubs in lead

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes after the other

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
an able person is clever

explanation.surface: A clever player backs up the clubs suit while holding the lead in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical lead is a flexible insulated wire, which is a cable.

clue.text: Group of aquatic creatures circling new water feature

indicators.note: the group goes round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a pod is a group of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A school of fish swims round and round a newly built garden water feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A small still body of water, often in a garden, is an ornamental water feature.

clue.text: Disillusioned vets might admit to this particular dislike

parts.words: Disillusioned vets might admit to this
parts.note: vets care for animals kept as companions; a disillusioned one might confess to loathing them

explanation.surface: Jaded veterinary surgeons might own up to a particular thing they can't stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are read literally: the animals vets treat, and the feeling of a disillusioned vet towards them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear that particularly irritates someone is their special, most personal dislike.

clue.text: Horse and badger

definitions.meaning: to badger is to pester someone persistently

explanation.surface: A horse and a badger, two animals side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an old horse and to pester persistently, as badger does as a verb.

clue.text: Inflammatory complaint on The Observer's cover

definitions.text: Inflammatory complaint on The Observer's cover

parts.words: Inflammatory complaint on The Observer's cover
parts.note: the observer is the eye and its cover the eyelid, where a small inflamed swelling can form

explanation.surface: An angry letter of complaint is splashed across the front page of The Observer newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, so 'cover' reads as its front page; really the observer is an eye and its cover an eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an inflamed swelling on the edge of an eyelid, a minor ailment of the eye's covering.

clue.text: A bad smell in theatre creates disruption

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the word for theatre

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
BO is body odour, a bad smell

explanation.surface: A foul odour wafting through the theatre wrecks the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately damaging or obstructing something is a way of causing disruption.

clue.text: Case of cider safe to consume — honest!

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: food fit to eat is edible

explanation.surface: Someone insists, with hand on heart, that a case of cider is fine to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Credible means believable or trustworthy, close in sense to honest.

clue.text: Keen opera singer making return

indicators.note: returning means the word for the singer is read backwards

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic opera singer stages a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid fan is eager and enthusiastic, a synonym of keen.

clue.text: Senior police officer reformed prison etc

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior police officer has overhauled the prisons and similar institutions.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a police rank above sergeant, a senior officer in British forces.

clue.text: Cook to catch geese, stuffing with European dairy product

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are stuffed with one more letter placed inside
to cook figures is to rework them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: go and catch some geese, then stuff them with something from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' turns TO CATCH GEESE into COTTAGECHESE, and 'stuffing with' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft lumpy curd cheese made from milk is a dairy product.

clue.text: Wrong tone to adversely affect digital growth

indicators.note: the letters of tone are put in the wrong order

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or affect badly

explanation.surface: Speaking in the wrong tone can do harm to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are fingers and toes, and the nail on a toe is something that grows from one.

clue.text: Vault over most of ice that's hidden

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: a crypt is an underground vault

indicators.note: most of the word ice means dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone vaults over an icy patch they couldn't see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' looks like a verb, a leap over the ice, but it is the underground chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means mysterious or obscure, with its meaning concealed, so hidden.

clue.text: Previously held in detention centre

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the words that follow, spanning their join

explanation.surface: Someone was previously held in a detention centre.
explanation.definitionFit: At one time in the past, formerly, means previously.

clue.text: One travelling much lighter, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is spoken, and the answer is what it sounds like

parts.note: way means much, as in way better, and fairer means lighter in colour

explanation.surface: A traveller goes on the road with a far lighter pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller on foot is a wayfarer, one who travels the roads.

clue.text: Wife and husband scoff grain

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A married couple tuck into a meal of cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cereal crop ground into flour, a kind of grain.

clue.text: A relatively short distance in train

parts.note: a foot is a short unit of length

explanation.surface: Someone notes that it is only a short way to the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans in train are already under way, and things under way are in progress.

clue.text: Decorative item of heraldic gold: call National Trust

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
to call something is to name it
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity that owns stately homes

explanation.surface: A collector rings the National Trust about a decorative heirloom bearing a gold coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A knick-knack or trinket put on display for show is a decoration.

clue.text: Eggs run out before start of Easter

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the next in the answer

parts.note: RO is the cricket abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The eggs have run out before Easter even begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish eggs, the mass of spawn in a female fish, are called by this name.

clue.text: Loathe keeping promise

indicators.note: the word Loathe keeps the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Someone hates having to keep a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn vow or sworn pledge is a promise.

clue.text: Processed cereal for breakfast, perhaps

definitions.meaning: ground grain such as oatmeal or cornmeal
breakfast is one example of an occasion when food is eaten

explanation.surface: Factory-made cereal, the kind eaten at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both coarsely ground grain and an occasion of eating, of which breakfast is one.

clue.text: Antisocial cat comes back and I go off

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: milk that goes off turns sour

explanation.surface: An unfriendly cat returns home and its owner leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means reserved and saying little, so unsociable or antisocial in manner.
